overview: Insurance Renewal Retention Prioritisation addresses operational records arrive through different systems, supervisors reconstruct evidence manually, and decisions are difficult to audit in insurance operations. The first proof of value uses policy tenure, renewal quotes and service interactions. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is renewal retention by customer cohort, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: policy tenure, renewal quotes and service interactions; define renewal retention by customer cohort and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Chief Claims Officer / Chief Underwriter.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including line-by-line reconciliations against known business transactions.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for renewal retention by customer cohort
